transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-17 11:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording: yes

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, and Omar and Leah from our solutions team are with me. How's everybody doing?
[00:07] Daniel Park: Good—thanks. Busy week but excited to see this.
[00:09] Tom Ruiz: Yeah hi, Tom here. We'll be mostly listening — Aisha and Daniel will dive into the technical details.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda: I'll do a 5–7 minute framing on product and pricing models, Omar will demo the hosted embeddings + reranker flow, Leah will show the console and Optimize suggestions. Then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:27] Daniel Park: Sounds great. We're interested in two things: relevance quality for our search UI and predictable latency under peak load. Also curious about cost sensitivity.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Got it. Omar, you want to take it away?
[00:39] Omar Reyes: Yup. So quick caveat, I'll call the endpoints out by shorthand — embeddings endpoint and reranker endpoint. The embeddings endpoint returns 768 or 1536-d vectors depending on model, and the reranker takes the candidate set and returns scores plus optional re-ranked text. I'll share the request/response in the chat.
[00:57] [screen share starts] 
[01:05] Omar Reyes: Here is a simple flow: user query -> dense vector via embeddings endpoint -> nearest neighbors from your vector DB -> pass topN to reranker endpoint with original query -> get scored results (score, explanation, tokens).
[01:20] Aisha Khan: When you say explanation, is that like salience highlights?
[01:23] Omar Reyes: We return a brief match snippet and sometimes a token-level attention map, though attention map names vary by model — transcriptions sometimes call it attention, but it's really a salience score.
[01:33] Daniel Park: For our catalog search, we usually do 50 nearest neighbors then a rerank to top 5. Any recommended N?
[01:39] Leah Patel: Most clients keep candidates between 20–100 depending on how expensive the reranker is. Redwood Optimize will recommend N based on historical query lengths and latency SLOs — it balances cost and recall.
[01:51] [02:05] Omar Reyes: Demo time. Hitting our hosted embeddings endpoint with a sample product query: 'lightweight hiking jacket women's'. You can see network latency ~35ms to Redwood endpoint from our region. The embedding payload is small, 2KB. Returned vector posted to local Milvus for NN search. Then we call reranker with top40 candidates — rerank call returns in ~120ms in this run.
[02:28] Aisha Khan: 120ms for rerank — what's the token budget on that?
[02:32] Omar Reyes: This run used a mid-size model, ~3B equivalent, with kv-cache optimizations and quantization Q4; tokens were average query + candidate text ~200 tokens. If you use a smaller reranker or a distilled model, you can push rerank under 80ms.
[02:47] Priya Menon: Can you show the console where we pick models?
[02:50] Leah Patel: Sure. In the Console -> Models tab you can pin model versions, see per-model latency distributions, and Optimize gives suggestions like 'switch reranker to quantized-v2 for 30% cost savings at ~5% relevance delta'.
[03:06] Tom Ruiz: How accurate are those Optimize recommendations? Do you run them on our data?
[03:10] Leah Patel: Initially Optimize uses global heuristics and the model profiles from our benchmark corpus. For higher-confidence recs we run a small calibration on a sample of your queries — which we recommend during POC. That gives per-customer suggestions with expected delta numbers.
[03:23] [03:40] Daniel Park: Security — we need VPC peering and KMS for keys. Also SOC2 report and audit logs for token-level usage.
[03:49] Maya Chen: Yes. For Private deployments we support VPC options; for Hosted we offer customer VPC peering or PrivateLink in supported regions. We have KMS integrations for data at rest; and long-form audit logs shipped to your SIEM. I'll attach the SOC2 summary and the data handling docs after the call.
[04:06] Aisha Khan: Is there a way to redact PII from the texts we send to reranker so it doesn't persist?
[04:10] Omar Reyes: Good question. We support configurable retention policies and on-write scrubbing via webhook processors or pre-processing on your side. For hosted API, you can enable automatic ephemeral mode where payloads are not stored beyond processing.
[04:22] [04:40] Daniel Park: What about rate limits and burst behavior? We can have spikes during sales pushes.
[04:45] Leah Patel: Hosted tier has soft rate limits and burst capacity; Dedicated reserve pools are best for predictable peak throughput. Also you can configure autoscale rules for Reserved capacity. If you need hard SLAs for latency at scale, Dedicated or Private are recommended.
[04:59] [05:20] Omar Reyes: Back to demo — I'm going to show how reranker returns explainability snippet. Here's a query 'waterproof boots narrow toe' — the reranker returns top1 with score 0.87 and a short reason 'matches waterproof membrane + narrow toe box in spec'. The UI exposes that via the explain field for downstream filtering.
[05:40] Aisha Khan: That field could help us drive personalization logic. Any cost for explainability?
[05:45] Omar Reyes: Slightly more compute since we materialize an explanation, but it's small relative to full rerank. Optimize will show cost delta when enabling explain.
[05:53] [06:10] Daniel Park: Curious about embeddings dimensionality choices — we have embeddings stored at 1024 dims now.
[06:15] Omar Reyes: Our embeddings models support 768, 1024, 1536 variants. Usually higher dims give marginal gains for complex semantics but increase vector DB cost. For your catalog size (~2M items), 1024 is reasonable. We'll test both during pilot.
[06:30] Priya Menon: Any examples of customers switching to lower-dim to save cost?
[06:34] Leah Patel: Sure — one retail customer reduced from 1536->1024 and saw <1.5% relevance drop but 30% vector storage savings. We can provide those anonymized benchmarks.
[06:45] [07:00] Tom Ruiz: On the reranker side, how do you handle model fallbacks if our primary reranker hits capacity?
[07:05] Omar Reyes: Smart routing can fallback to a cheaper reranker or to a heuristic scoring tier (lexical signals + embeddings score) to preserve latency. You can configure policy: strict (fail hard) vs degrade (fallback).
[07:18] Aisha Khan: Can we route only some users to a more expensive reranker for experiments?
[07:21] Leah Patel: Yep — we support canary and A/B route policies in the Console. You can split by token, header, or user bucket and collect per-route metrics.
[07:34] [07:50] Daniel Park: Let's talk POC scope — we want to test accuracy improvements for product search, measure end-to-end latency, and estimate cost at 5k qps? Wait, 5k/day sorry.
[07:59] Maya Chen: 5k/day is straightforward. For POC we typically: 1) run a 1–2k query benchmark against a sample corpus to get baseline metrics; 2) run rerank variations (mid-model vs distilled) and record latency/cost; 3) iterate until we find best cost/quality point.
[08:17] Omar Reyes: I'll propose we run three runs: embeddings only (dot-product recall), rerank with mid-size model, rerank with distilled reranker. We'll report MRR/NDCG + p95 latency + estimated monthly cost.
[08:31] Aisha Khan: That would be perfect. We'll share sample queries and docs after.
[08:35] [09:00] Maya Chen: Okay quick note on pricing — hosted per-request pricing: embeddings priced per 1k vectors, rerank billed per token + a flat routing fee. For pilots we provide trial credits. I'll send detailed numbers.
[09:12] Tom Ruiz: Are there any contractual minimums for Dedicated?
[09:16] Maya Chen: Dedicated requires reserved capacity commitments — we can discuss numbers in the next meeting once we have usage projections.
[09:22] [09:40] Aisha Khan: Implementation question — we use Milvus today. Any gotchas?
[09:44] Omar Reyes: Milvus is a common choice. We recommend storing raw text + vector IDs and using filtering at NN stage to keep candidates relevant. One caveat is vector size and index type — we'll surface recommended index params in our integration doc.
[09:57] [10:10] Daniel Park: Can Redwood host the reranker in our VPC?
[10:14] Leah Patel: For Private deployments yes; for Hosted we do VPC peering or PrivateLink to avoid egress via public internet. We can also deploy a dedicated VPC connector for higher isolation.
[10:25] [10:40] Omar Reyes: I'm going to run a quick live benchmark using LucentPath sample (anonymized) — this is a canned run we've prepared. Note: network conditions vary. Starting 1k queries at 5qps.
[10:55] [11:10] [benchmark runs, partial metrics streamed]
[11:20] Omar Reyes: Results: embeddings latency p50 ~25ms, p95 70ms; reranker p50 110ms, p95 240ms. Cost estimate at 5k/day: ~$1,200/month for mid-size reranker + embeddings storage ~ $450/month — ballpark.
[11:35] Daniel Park: p95 240ms for rerank is a bit high for us, we want <150ms. Can we tune?
[11:40] Omar Reyes: Yes — you can shrink candidate N, use a distilled reranker, or enable batching for steady load which reduces per-item latency at throughput cost. Also region selection matters; pushing to nearer region reduces network.
[11:53] Aisha Khan: Is there a way to get token-level cost breakdown?
[11:56] Leah Patel: Console -> Billing -> Token breakdown shows per-route token counts and estimated cost per thousand tokens. We'll share a screenshot.
[12:05] [12:20] Maya Chen: Ok let's summarize and next steps. Omar will run the 1k benchmark on LucentPath sample and provide p50/p95/cost/MRR. I'll send pricing + SOC2 docs and pilot contract. We should schedule the POC kickoff next Tue.
[12:34] Daniel Park: Great. Quick clarifying Q: for ephemeral mode, are logs suppressed entirely?
[12:37] Leah Patel: In ephemeral mode we don't persist payloads; we still generate audit trails for request metadata (IDs, timestamps) but not text bodies.
[12:46] Tom Ruiz: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[12:48] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with materials.
[12:52] End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript with occasional mislabeling; some product names were approximated (e.g., Quant4 referred to as Q4), and attention map phrasing sometimes inconsistent.
